title: Tuning kV and kP
summary: Feedforward first, then add feedback, watching the graph.

say.never: PID here has two parts added together. **Feedforward** is a smart first guess: "this speed usually needs about this much power." **Feedback** is a correction on top: the bigger the error, the bigger the push. kV scales the guess and kP scales the correction.
say.bit: PID here is the feedforward guess **plus** a correction that grows with the error.

marks.label: feedforward: the power to hold the speed

say.never: Hold down **Ctrl** and tap **P**. A small search box pops up at the top. Type `ShooterConstants`, then press **Enter**. It finds any file by its name, so you never have to dig through folders.
say.bit: Press **Ctrl+P**, type `ShooterConstants` and press Enter. Quick Open finds any file by name, so you never have to dig through folders.

say.never: Search for `FLYWHEEL_KV`. Set `FLYWHEEL_CONTROL = FEEDFORWARD`. Then try kV values 0.05, then 0.10, then 0.12. Restart each time and watch the graph to see which gets the flywheel closest to its target.
say.bit: Search for `FLYWHEEL_KV`. Set `FLYWHEEL_CONTROL = FEEDFORWARD` and try kV 0.05, 0.10, 0.12, restarting each time.

say.never: Hold **U**, then tap **K** (A) to launch a game piece. Feedforward never notices the dip. Look at **AdvantageScope**, the graphing tool. Type `FlywheelVelocity` in its search box. Find **Subsystem/Shooter/FlywheelVelocity** in the list and drag it with your mouse onto the **Left Axis** of the graph. Then move the robot and watch the line change.

say.never: Now switch to `PID` and keep your best kV. Raise `FLYWHEEL_KP` through 0.05, then 0.2, then 1.0. After a shot, the flywheel should now recover faster. Be careful: too big a kP and a real robot starts to buzz.
